title: They Walked Up the Mountain Together, But Only One Knew the Cost
paragraphs: They Walked Up the Mountain Together, But Only One Knew the Cost
When God asks for something you love, it does not feel holy at first. It feels like loss. It feels like confusion. It feels like silence where answers should be.
That is where this story begins.
Not on the mountain.
But in the heart of a father who heard a voice he could not ignore.

“וַיֹּאמֶר קַח־נָא אֶת־בִּנְךָ אֶת־יְחִידְךָ אֲשֶׁר־אָהַבְתָּ אֶת־יִצְחָק...”
Vayomer: Kach-na et-bincha, et-yechidcha, asher-ahavta, et-Yitzchak…
“And He said, ‘Take your son, your only son, whom you love—Isaac…’” (Genesis 22:2)
God did not soften it.
He named the love.

Your son.
Your only one.
The one you love.
Because this was never just about sacrifice.
It was about trust.
Abraham did not argue. That alone should disturb you. No debate. No delay. Just obedience that cut deeper than any knife he would later carry.
And somewhere behind him… Isaac followed.
No thunder. No warning. Just footsteps.
Can you imagine that silence between them?

A father carrying fire.
A son carrying wood.
And between them… a question waiting to be asked.
They walked long enough for the weight of the journey to settle into Isaac’s spirit. He wasn’t a child too young to notice. He saw patterns. He had watched sacrifices before.
Something was missing.
And finally, the silence broke.

“וַיֹּאמֶר יִצְחָק אֶל־אַבְרָהָם אָבִיו… הִנֵּה הָאֵשׁ וְהָעֵצִים וְאַיֵּה הַשֶּׂה לְעֹלָה?”
Vayomer Yitzchak el-Avraham aviv… hineh ha’esh veha’etzim, ve’ayei haseh le’olah?
“Isaac spoke to Abraham his father… ‘Behold the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?’” (Genesis 22:7)
That question still echoes.
Where is the lamb?
Every believer has asked it in some form.

Where is God in this pain?
Where is the answer I was promised?
Where is the provision when everything feels like it’s falling apart?
Abraham’s response was not explanation.
It was prophecy.

“אֱלֹהִים יִרְאֶה־לּוֹ הַשֶּׂה לְעֹלָה בְּנִי”
Elohim yir’eh-lo haseh le’olah, b’ni.
“God will provide for Himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” (Genesis 22:8)
He didn’t say God might.
He didn’t say God could.
He said God will.
But notice this… Abraham said more than he understood.
Because in that moment, there was no lamb.
Only wood.
Only fire.
Only a son.
And here is where the story becomes unbearable… and holy at the same time.
Isaac was not forced.
There is no record of struggle.
No resistance.
He allowed himself to be bound.

“וַיַּעֲקֹד אֶת־יִצְחָק בְּנוֹ”
Vaya’akod et-Yitzchak beno.
“And he bound Isaac his son…” (Genesis 22:9)
This is where the name “Akedah” comes from—the binding.
Isaac trusted his father.
Abraham trusted his God.
And heaven watched both.
Do you see it?

A son carrying wood up a hill…
A father willing to offer what he loves most…
Silence before intervention…
This is not just Abraham’s story.
This is a shadow of something greater.
Because centuries later, another Son would walk up a hill carrying wood on His back.
Not questioning.
Not resisting.
Not escaping.
And this time… there would be no substitute.

“ὁ ἀμνὸς τοῦ θεοῦ”
Ho amnos tou Theou
“The Lamb of God” (John 1:29)
Jesus.
Where Isaac was spared, Christ was not.
Where Abraham stopped, God the Father did not.
Where a ram was caught in the thicket, Jesus became the sacrifice.
And suddenly… Abraham’s words make sense in a way they never had before.
God will provide the Lamb.
Not just for Abraham.
For all of us.
Because the real scandal was never the command to sacrifice Isaac.
The real scandal is that God would give His own Son for people who would question Him, doubt Him, run from Him… and still be loved by Him.

“ὃς γε τοῦ ἰδίου υἱοῦ οὐκ ἐφείσατο…”
Hos ge tou idiou huiou ouk epheisato…
“He who did not spare His own Son…” (Romans 8:32)
Sit with that.
God did not spare His Son so He could spare you.
This is where the mountain becomes personal.
Because maybe you’re walking your own version of that road right now.

Carrying something heavy.
Asking questions that feel unanswered.
Trusting God while not fully understanding Him.
Be honest.
This hit harder than you expected.
You’re not alone on that mountain.
And the story didn’t end in sacrifice.
It ended in provision.

“וַיִּקְרָא אַבְרָהָם… יְהוָה יִרְאֶה”
Vayikra Avraham… Adonai Yireh.
“And Abraham called the name of that place, ‘The LORD Will Provide.’” (Genesis 22:14)
Not might provide.
Will provide.
That name still stands.
Even in your unanswered prayers.
Even in your breaking point.
Even in your confusion.
God sees.
God provides.
God redeems.
And if this stirred something in your heart, don’t keep it to yourself.
They need this reminder more than you realize.
You will need to come back to it when faith feels fragile.
It’s not about supporting a page. It’s about committing to discipleship, growth, and staying anchored in Christ daily.
This isn’t just content.
This is nourishment.
This is accountability.
This is growth.
Because at some point, inspiration isn’t enough.
You need transformation.
And it always begins the same way…

On a mountain.
With a question.
And a God who already has the answer.
He never asked Abraham for Isaac to take him away.
He asked for Isaac to show Abraham who He truly was.
